rationale: Soil zinc availability governs crop zinc density and is the basis of the GeoNutrition soil-to-human hypothesis (Gashu et al. 2021 Nature; Joy/Broadley work in Malawi and Ethiopia).
Soil extractable iron as the analogous pathway for iron; weaker evidence than zinc but the same mechanism.

Zinc and iron uptake are strongly pH-dependent; alkaline soils immobilise both. pH is the standard modifier in the soil-crop literature. NOTE: iSDAsoil pH is not present in the raster exports, so SoilGrids carries this pathway alone.
Organic carbon indexes general soil fertility and nutrient retention.
SoilGrids equivalents retained alongside iSDAsoil so the arm is not hostage to one product, given the two disagree in places.
Greenness as an integrated proxy for agricultural productivity and food availability; standard in food-security prediction.
EVI is less saturation-prone than NDVI in high-biomass areas.
NPP is the closest remotely-sensed analogue of agricultural output.
Rainfall is the dominant yield constraint in rainfed systems across these four countries.
Actual evapotranspiration and climatic water deficit capture growing-season water stress better than raw rainfall.
Night LST separates agro-ecological zones and correlates with vector ecology.
Elevation structures temperature, cropping system and malaria transmission simultaneously.
Travel time to care governs access to supplementation, fortification and antenatal services.
Night-time lights as the standard proxy for local economic activity and electrification.
Urban households have more diverse but more processed diets; urbanicity is a first-order determinant.
Population scale conditions market size and service provision.
Cumulative human modification indexes land-use intensity.
Grazing land proxies livestock density and therefore access to animal-source foods, the key source of bioavailable iron, zinc and B12.
Cereal- versus root-dominated staples differ sharply in micronutrient density and in phytate content, which inhibits absorption.
Cropland and tree cover fractions distinguish farming systems.
Maternal education is among the most consistently replicated determinants of child nutritional status.
Enteric infection and environmental enteropathy impair absorption and drive nutrient loss.
Wealth conditions dietary quality and diversity.
Malaria drives anaemia and inflammation, which confound and cause iron deficiency.
Dietary diversity and early breastfeeding initiation are core IYCF determinants.
ANC contact is the delivery channel for iron-folate supplementation.
